a:r.a:t: Smart India Hackathon 2026 · PS 26016 · Ministry of Rural Development, Dept. of Land Resources · Team CyberPookies
A parcel moves through notification, survey, objections, valuation, approval, award and possession — each with its own deadline, documents and officer.
No one holds the whole chain.
Status sits in district spreadsheets and project-office files, so the Ministry has to ask states for a return to learn anything.
The landowner is outside the system.
There is no way to check where a survey number stands, or why it stopped.
Delay is found after it happens
— at project review, not on the day a parcel starts slipping past its stage deadline.
Money is tracked apart from status.
“How much is still unpaid?” is a manual exercise.
One shared parcel record. Two portals. Seven gated stages.
Stage, history, documents, objections, compensation, owner and map boundary live on one record — officials and landowners read the same record.
A gate, not a status field.
A parcel advances only when that stage’s required documents are verified and no objection is open. The rule is enforced in code, not in a circular.
A deterministic 0–100 risk score ranks every parcel; the Action Center names the responsible officer and the exact next action.
Each history entry is SHA-256 chained to the one before it — a back-dated edit visibly breaks the chain.
Search by survey number — no account, no app, no visit to the office.
Hindi + English UI, voice search and read-aloud for low-literacy users, and a data-saver mode that drops map tiles on weak district networks.
SMS drafted in the language on record — Hindi, Marathi or English — at every stage change and objection update.
The same code runs on in-memory data or on PostgreSQL, so a district can pilot it before anything is bought.
Scope-aware printable reports, plus per-stage duration against SLA — so the slow stage is visible, not inferred.
THE STATUTORY WORKFLOW WE MODEL — RFCTLARR Act, 2013
required documents verified + no open objection → advance. Miss either and the parcel is held, the SLA clock keeps running, and its risk score rises.
